     2→
     3→> Atomic development workflow for building Bivvy.
     4→
     5→<steps>
     6→  <step number="1" id="specification">
     7→    <title>Specification</title>
     8→    <goal>Define the contract your code must fulfill before writing implementation.</goal>
     9→    <instructions>
    10→      <instruction>
    11→        Define the Behavior: Create test files first. Tests are the specification.
    12→        <conditional>
    13→          <condition>Test files already exist</condition>
    14→          <action>Update tests to match the new/changed behavior</action>
    15→        </conditional>
    16→      </instruction>
    17→      <instruction>
    18→        <command>cargo test --all-features</command>
    19→        <expected>All new or updated tests should FAIL</expected>
    20→        <rationale>Failing tests prove they're actually testing new logic, not passing by accident.</rationale>
    21→      </instruction>
    22→    </instructions>
    23→    <gate>
    24→      <condition>New tests fail for the right reasons</condition>
    25→      <on_fail>Refine your tests until they correctly specify the behavior</on_fail>
    26→    </gate>
    27→  </step>
    28→
    29→  <step number="2" id="implementation">
    30→    <title>Implementation</title>
    31→    <goal>Write the minimum code to make tests pass.</goal>
    32→    <prerequisite ref="specification">Failing tests from specification step</prerequisite>
    33→    <instructions>
    34→      <instruction>
    35→        Write the Code: Implement only what's needed to pass the tests. Resist adding "nice to have" features.
    36→      </instruction>
    37→      <instruction>
    38→        Keep it Simple: If you're writing more code than tests require, stop and reconsider.
    39→      </instruction>
    40→    </instructions>
    41→    <gate>
    42→      <condition>All tests pass</condition>
    43→      <on_fail>Continue implementing or fix bugs until green</on_fail>
    44→    </gate>
    45→  </step>
    46→
    47→  <step number="3" id="documentation">
    48→    <title>Documentation</title>
    49→    <goal>Document while context is fresh. User-facing and dev-facing docs are separate concerns.</goal>
    50→    <prerequisite ref="implementation">Tests passing</prerequisite>
    51→    <instructions>
    52→      <instruction>
    53→        Rustdoc Comments: Add `///` doc comments to all public items (structs, functions, modules). This is the primary form of API documentation.
    54→      </instruction>
    55→      <instruction>
    56→        User-Facing Docs: Update `docs/` if adding commands, config options, or user-visible features. These are Starlight pages written for end users — never reference internals.
    57→      </instruction>
    58→      <instruction>
    59→        Source READMEs: Update or create `README.md` in source directories (e.g., `src/cli/README.md`) when adding or changing subsystem design, architecture, or guiding principles.
    60→      </instruction>
    61→      <instruction>
    62→        Inline Comments: Add comments only where the "why" isn't obvious from the code.
    63→      </instruction>
    64→      <instruction>
    65→        Verify Docs Build: Confirm documentation compiles without errors.
    66→        <command>cargo doc --no-deps --all-features</command>
    67→        <expected>No documentation errors</expected>
    68→      </instruction>
    69→    </instructions>
    70→    <boundaries>
    71→      <rule>Developer docs go in source tree (rustdoc + source READMEs), never in `docs/`</rule>
    72→      <rule>User-facing docs go in `docs/`, never in source READMEs</rule>
    73→    </boundaries>
    74→    <anti-patterns>
    75→      <anti-pattern>Documenting "what" the code does (the code should show that)</anti-pattern>
    76→      <anti-pattern>Leaving documentation for later (it won't happen)</anti-pattern>
    77→      <anti-pattern>Over-commenting obvious code</anti-pattern>
    78→      <anti-pattern>Putting developer architecture docs in `docs/`</anti-pattern>
    79→      <anti-pattern>Putting user-facing guides in source READMEs</anti-pattern>
    80→    </anti-patterns>
    81→  </step>
    82→
    83→  <step number="4" id="linting">
    84→    <title>Static Quality Gate (Linting)</title>
    85→    <goal>Catch issues before they become problems.</goal>
    86→    <prerequisite ref="documentation">Implementation and documentation complete</prerequisite>
    87→    <instructions>
    88→      <instruction>
    89→        <command>cargo fmt -- --check</command>
    90→        <expected>No formatting differences</expected>
    91→        <fix>cargo fmt</fix>
    92→      </instruction>
    93→      <instruction>
    94→        <command>cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings</command>
    95→        <expected>No warnings or errors</expected>
    96→        <rationale>Warnings today become bugs tomorrow. Zero tolerance. Flags match CI.</rationale>
    97→      </instruction>
    98→    </instructions>
    99→    <gate>
   100→      <condition>Both commands pass with zero output</condition>
   101→      <on_fail goto="implementation">Fix all issues. Return to implementation if code changes are needed.</on_fail>
   102→    </gate>
   103→  </step>
   104→
   105→  <step number="5" id="testing">
   106→    <title>Verification Gate (Full Test Suite)</title>
   107→    <goal>Ensure nothing is broken.</goal>
   108→    <prerequisite ref="linting">Linting passes</prerequisite>
   109→    <critical>
   110→      ALWAYS run `cargo test --all-features` without filters. NEVER use:
   111→      - cargo test some_name
   112→      - cargo test module::
   113→      - cargo test --lib
   114→      The ENTIRE test suite must pass with all features. "X filtered out" means you ran it wrong.
   115→      The --all-features flag matches CI - skipping it locally may cause CI failures.
   116→    </critical>
   117→    <instructions>
   118→      <instruction>
   119→        <command>cargo test --all-features</command>
   120→        <expected>All tests pass (new and existing), 0 filtered out</expected>
   121→      </instruction>
   122→      <instruction>
   123→        <command>cargo llvm-cov --all-features --fail-under-lines 90</command>
   124→        <expected>Coverage at or above 90%</expected>
   125→        <conditional>
   126→          <condition>cargo-llvm-cov not installed</condition>
   127→          <action>Skip coverage check locally; CI will enforce</action>
   128→        </conditional>
   129→      </instruction>
   130→    </instructions>
   131→    <gate>
   132→      <condition>All tests pass, coverage threshold met</condition>
   133→      <on_fail goto="implementation">Do not proceed with failing tests.</on_fail>
   134→    </gate>
   135→  </step>
   136→
   137→  <step number="6" id="build">
   138→    <title>Integration Gate (Build Verification)</title>
   139→    <goal>Confirm production readiness.</goal>
   140→    <prerequisite ref="testing">All tests passing</prerequisite>
   141→    <instructions>
   142→      <instruction>
   143→        <command>cargo build --all-targets --all-features</command>
   144→        <expected>Build succeeds with no warnings</expected>
   145→        <rationale>RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" in CI means any warning fails the build. Flags match CI.</rationale>
   146→      </instruction>
   147→      <instruction>
   148→        <command>cargo build --release</command>
   149→        <expected>Release build succeeds</expected>
   150→        <rationale>Catches release-only issues (optimizations, LTO problems).</rationale>
   151→      </instruction>
   152→    </instructions>
   153→    <gate>
   154→      <condition>Both builds succeed silently</condition>
   155→      <on_fail goto="linting">Treat warnings as errors. Return to linting or implementation until clean.</on_fail>
   156→    </gate>
   157→  </step>
   158→
   159→  <step number="7" id="commit">
   160→    <title>The Atomic Commit</title>
   161→    <goal>Create a single, complete unit of work.</goal>
   162→    <prerequisite ref="build">All gates passed (lint, test, build)</prerequisite>
   163→    <instructions>
   164→      <instruction>
   165→        Stage Selectively: Add only the files related to this change.
   166→        <command>git add [specific files]</command>
   167→        <anti-pattern>git add -A (may include unrelated changes)</anti-pattern>
   168→      </instruction>
   169→      <instruction>
   170→        Write the Message: Explain WHY, not just WHAT.
   171→        <format>
   172→          <line>Short description in imperative mood, 50 chars or less</line>
   173→          <line></line>
   174→          <line>Longer explanation of why this change was made,</line>
   175→          <line>what problem it solves, and any important context.</line>
   176→          <line>Wrap at 72 characters.</line>
   177→        </format>
   178→        <rules>
   179→          <rule>Imperative mood ("Add feature" not "Added feature")</rule>
   180→          <rule>Capitalize first letter, no period at end</rule>
   181→          <rule>No type prefixes (no "feat:", "fix:", etc.)</rule>
   182→        </rules>
   183→      </instruction>
   184→      <instruction>
   185→        Verify Atomicity: This commit should be independently checkable, buildable, testable, and documented.
   186→      </instruction>
   187→    </instructions>
   188→    <gate>
   189→      <condition>Commit contains code + tests + docs for one logical change</condition>
   190→      <on_fail>Split into smaller commits or add missing pieces</on_fail>
   191→    </gate>
   192→  </step>
   193→
   194→  <step number="8" id="post-commit">
   195→    <title>Post-Commit Verification</title>
   196→    <goal>Confirm the commit didn't break anything.</goal>
   197→    <prerequisite ref="commit">Commit created</prerequisite>
   198→    <instructions>
   199→      <instruction>
   200→        <command>cargo test</command>
   201→        <expected>Still passing after commit</expected>
   202→      </instruction>
   203→      <instruction>
   204→        <command>cargo build</command>
   205→        <expected>Build succeeds with no warnings</expected>
   206→      </instruction>
   207→      <instruction>
   208→        <command>git log -1 --stat</command>
   209→        <rationale>Review what was actually committed</rationale>
   210→      </instruction>
   211→    </instructions>
   212→  </step>
   213→
   214→  <step number="9" id="transition">
   215→    <title>Transition</title>
   216→    <goal>Clean context switch to next task.</goal>
   217→    <instructions>
   218→      <instruction>
   219→        Clean Slate: Clear your mental context. The previous task is done.
   220→      </instruction>
   221→      <instruction goto="specification">
   222→        Next Task: Pick the next item from your backlog and return to specification.
   223→      </instruction>
   224→    </instructions>
   225→  </step>
   226→</steps>

1→# Bivvy Development Guidelines
     2→
     3→> Cross-language development environment setup automation, built in Rust.
     4→
     5→## Project Overview
     6→
     7→Bivvy is a CLI tool that replaces ad-hoc `bin/setup` scripts with a declarative YAML configuration and a polished interactive CLI experience. It uses a **Template Registry** instead of hardcoded language logic, allowing user overrides at every level.
     8→
     9→<references>
    10→  <reference path="plans/bivvy-plan.md">Full implementation specification</reference>
    11→  <reference path="plans/README.md">Milestone overview and status</reference>
    12→  <reference path=".claude/bivvy-dev-workflow.md">Development workflow (FOLLOW THIS)</reference>
    13→</references>
    14→
    15→## Development Workflow
    16→
    17→**Follow the workflow defined in `.claude/bivvy-dev-workflow.md` for all development work.**
    18→
    19→<workflow-summary>
    20→  <step ref="specification">Write failing tests first</step>
    21→  <step ref="implementation">Implement minimum code to pass tests</step>
    22→  <step ref="documentation">Document while context is fresh (rustdoc for APIs, `docs/` for user-facing changes, source READMEs for design)</step>
    23→  <step ref="linting">Pass `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy`</step>
    24→  <step ref="testing">Pass all tests with >90% coverage</step>
    25→  <step ref="build">Verify clean build</step>
    26→  <step ref="commit">Create atomic commit with code + tests + docs</step>
    27→</workflow-summary>
    28→
    29→<verification-commands>
    30→  <command>cargo doc --no-deps --all-features</command>
    31→  <command>cargo fmt -- --check</command>
    32→  <command>cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings</command>
    33→  <command>cargo test --all-features</command>
    34→  <command>cargo build --all-targets --all-features</command>
    35→  <command>cargo build --release</command>
    36→  <command>cargo llvm-cov --all-features --fail-under-lines 90</command>
    37→</verification-commands>
    38→
    39→<critical>
    40→  ALWAYS run `cargo test --all-features` without any filters.
    41→
    42→  CORRECT:   cargo test --all-features
    43→  WRONG:     cargo test config
    44→  WRONG:     cargo test schema
    45→  WRONG:     cargo test --lib
    46→  WRONG:     cargo test some_module::
    47→
    48→  Every verification must run the ENTIRE test suite with all features.
    49→  Never filter to "just the relevant tests" - ALL tests must pass before every commit.
    50→
    51→  If you see "X filtered out" in test output, you ran the wrong command.
    52→
    53→  The --all-features and --all-targets flags match what CI runs. If you skip
    54→  them locally, you may push code that fails CI.
    55→</critical>
    56→
    57→<prohibited-behaviors>
    58→  <behavior>Skipping, disabling, or modifying tests to make them pass</behavior>
    59→  <behavior>Creating commits without accompanying tests</behavior>
    60→  <behavior>Moving on to other work when tests are failing</behavior>
    61→  <behavior>Large commits with multiple unrelated changes</behavior>
    62→  <behavior>Straying from the implementation plan without explicit approval</behavior>
    63→  <behavior>Filtering tests when not debugging (e.g., `cargo test config` instead of `cargo test`)</behavior>
    64→</prohibited-behaviors>
    65→
    66→## Architecture
    67→
    68→<philosophy>
    69→Bivvy is a **declarative orchestrator**, not a collection of hardcoded scripts:
    70→  <principle>Uses a Template Registry instead of hardcoded language logic</principle>
    71→  <principle>Optionally injects pre-defined YAML templates during `bivvy init`</principle>
    72→  <principle>Allows user overrides at every level</principle>
    73→  <principle>Tracks execution state to enable smart re-runs</principle>
    74→</philosophy>
    75→
    76→### Supported Platforms
    77→
    78→- macOS (arm64, x64)
    79→- Linux (arm64, x64)
    80→- Windows (x64)
    81→
    82→### Key Dependencies
    83→
    84→```toml
    85→clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive", "env"] }   # CLI framework
    86→dialoguer = "0.12"                                        # Interactive prompts
    87→indicatif = "0.18"                                        # Progress indicators
    88→console = "0.16"                                          # Terminal styling
    89→serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }          # Serialization
    90→marked_yaml = "0.8"                                       # YAML with source locations
    91→anyhow = "1"                                              # Error handling
    92→thiserror = "2"                                           # Custom errors
    93→git2 = "0.20"                                             # Git integration
    94→reqwest = { version = "0.13", features = ["blocking"] }   # HTTP client
    95→```
    96→
    97→### File Locations
    98→
    99→<file-structure>
   100→  <location name="project" path=".bivvy/">
   101→    <file>config.yml</file>
   102→    <file>config.local.yml (gitignored)</file>
   103→    <directory>templates/</directory>
   104→  </location>
   105→  <location name="system" path="~/.bivvy/">
   106→    <file>config.yml</file>
   107→    <directory>templates/</directory>
   108→    <directory>projects/{id}/</directory>
   109→    <directory>cache/</directory>
   110→  </location>
   111→</file-structure>
   112→
   113→## CLI Commands
   114→
   115→| Command | Description |
   116→|---------|-------------|
   117→| `bivvy` / `bivvy run` | Run default workflow |
   118→| `bivvy init` | Initialize configuration |
   119→| `bivvy status` | Pre-flight check |
   120→| `bivvy list` | Show steps and workflows |
   121→| `bivvy lint` | Validate configuration |
   122→| `bivvy last` | Show last run info |
   123→| `bivvy history` | Show execution history |
   124→
   125→## Configuration Schema
   126→
   127→```yaml
   128→app_name: "MyApp"
   129→
   130→settings:
   131→  default_output: verbose    # verbose | quiet | silent
   132→  logging: false
   133→
   134→steps:
   135→  step_name:
   136→    template: template_name  # OR define inline
   137→    command: "..."
   138→    depends_on: [other_step]
   139→    completed_check:
   140→      type: file_exists | command_succeeds | marker
   141→      path: "..."
   142→      command: "..."
   143→    watches:
   144→      - file_to_watch.lock
   145→
   146→workflows:
   147→  default:
   148→    steps: [step1, step2, step3]
   149→```
   150→
   151→## Documentation
   152→
   153→Bivvy has two distinct documentation audiences. Keep them separate.
   154→
   155→<documentation>
   156→  <audience name="user-facing" path="docs/">
   157→    <description>Pages served by Starlight on Bivvy's website. Written for end users.</description>
   158→    <rule>All user-facing documentation lives in `docs/`</rule>
   159→    <rule>Write for someone who has never seen the source code</rule>
   160→    <rule>Focus on what Bivvy does and how to use it, not how it's built</rule>
   161→    <rule>Follow the structure in `docs/SUMMARY.md`</rule>
   162→    <rule>When adding a new command, feature, or config option, add or update the corresponding `docs/` page</rule>
   163→  </audience>
   164→
   165→  <audience name="dev-facing" path="src/">
   166→    <description>Developer documentation lives inside the source tree. Written for contributors.</description>
   167→    <form name="rustdoc">
   168→      <rule>Add `///` and `//!` doc comments to all public items (structs, functions, modules)</rule>
   169→      <rule>Primary way to document what code does and how to use it</rule>
   170→    </form>
   171→    <form name="source-readmes">
   172→      <description>Higher-level `README.md` files in source directories that document subsystem design. Example: `src/ui/README.md` documents CLX design norms, color assignments, and spinner lifecycle.</description>
   173→      <rule>Place `README.md` files in source directories to document subsystem design (e.g., `src/cli/README.md`, `src/config/README.md`)</rule>
   174→      <rule>Cover: purpose, key modules/files, design decisions, testing guidance, guiding principles</rule>
   175→      <rule>Focus on the "why" and "how it fits together" — leave API details to rustdoc</rule>
   176→    </form>
   177→  </audience>
   178→
   179→  <boundaries>
   180→    <rule>Do NOT put developer documentation in `docs/` — that directory is exclusively for end users</rule>
   181→    <rule>Do NOT put user-facing documentation in source READMEs — point to `docs/` instead</rule>
   182→  </boundaries>
   183→</documentation>
   184→
   185→## Coding Standards
   186→
   187→<standards>
   188→  <standard name="error-handling">
   189→    <rule>Use `anyhow::Result` for application errors</rule>
   190→    <rule>Use `thiserror` for library/domain errors</rule>
   191→    <rule>Provide actionable error messages with context</rule>
   192→  </standard>
   193→
   194→  <standard name="output">
   195→    <rule>Support `--verbose`, `--quiet`, `--non-interactive` flags</rule>
   196→    <rule>Mask secrets in all output (`*_KEY`, `*_SECRET`, `*_TOKEN`, etc.)</rule>
   197→    <rule>Use spinners and progress indicators from `indicatif`</rule>
   198→  </standard>
   199→
   200→  <standard name="idempotency">
   201→    <rule>Steps should be safe to re-run</rule>
   202→    <rule>Use `completed_check` to detect if work is already done</rule>
   203→    <rule>Prompt before re-running completed steps (unless `--force`)</rule>
   204→  </standard>
   205→</standards>
   206→
   207→## Testing Patterns
   208→
   209→<test-layers>
   210→  <layer name="Unit" tools="cargo test" speed="Fast">
   211→    Individual functions, parsing, logic
   212→  </layer>
   213→  <layer name="Integration" tools="assert_cmd, tempfile" speed="Medium">
   214→    CLI commands, file I/O, config loading
   215→  </layer>
   216→  <layer name="Snapshot" tools="insta" speed="Fast">
   217→    CLI output format, error messages
   218→  </layer>
   219→</test-layers>
   220→
   221→<cli-testing>
   222→  Use `parse_from()` instead of `parse()` in tests and doc examples:
   223→
   224→  ```rust
   225→  // WRONG - reads actual process args, fails in tests
   226→  let cli = Cli::parse();
   227→
   228→  // CORRECT - explicit args, works in tests
   229→  let cli = Cli::parse_from(["bivvy", "run", "--verbose"]);
   230→  ```
   231→
   232→  This applies to:
   233→  - Unit tests for CLI parsing
   234→  - Doc tests / examples in rustdoc
   235→  - Any test that needs to verify CLI behavior
   236→
   237→  Only use `Cli::parse()` in the actual `main()` function.
   238→</cli-testing>
   239→
   240→<doc-test-guidelines>
   241→  Doc tests should be self-contained and runnable whenever possible.
   242→
   243→  PREFER runnable examples with real test fixtures:
   244→  ```rust
   245→  /// ```
   246→  /// use bivvy::config::load_merged_config;
   247→  /// use tempfile::TempDir;
   248→  /// use std::fs;
   249→  ///
   250→  /// // Create real test files
   251→  /// let temp = TempDir::new().unwrap();
   252→  /// fs::create_dir_all(temp.path().join(".bivvy")).unwrap();
   253→  /// fs::write(temp.path().join(".bivvy/config.yml"), "app_name: test").unwrap();
   254→  ///
   255→  /// // Test with real data
   256→  /// let config = load_merged_config(temp.path()).unwrap();
   257→  /// assert_eq!(config.app_name, Some("test".to_string()));
   258→  /// ```
   259→  ```
   260→
   261→  Use `no_run` ONLY for code that truly can't run in tests (interactive terminal
   262→  input, network calls to real servers, etc.):
   263→  ```rust
   264→  /// ```no_run
   265→  /// // Requires interactive terminal input
   266→  /// let answer = ui.prompt_confirm("Continue?")?;
   267→  /// ```
   268→  ```
   269→
   270→  Use `ignore` only for pseudocode that won't compile. Always explain why:
   271→  ```rust
   272→  /// ```ignore
   273→  /// // Pseudocode showing concept - yaml() helper doesn't exist
   274→  /// let config = yaml("key: value");
   275→  /// ```
   276→  ```
   277→
   278→  NEVER use `ignore` or `no_run` just because setup is tedious - use tempfile!
   279→</doc-test-guidelines>
   280→
   281→### Unit Test Example
   282→
   283→```rust
   284→#[cfg(test)]
   285→mod tests {
   286→    use super::*;
   287→
   288→    #[test]
   289→    fn deep_merge_replaces_at_conflict_point() {
   290→        // Test actual merge behavior
   291→    }
   292→}
   293→```
   294→
   295→### Integration Test Example
   296→
   297→```rust
   298→use assert_cmd::prelude::*;
   299→use predicates::prelude::*;
   300→use std::process::Command;
   301→use tempfile::TempDir;
   302→
   303→#[test]
   304→fn init_creates_config_file() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
   305→    let temp = TempDir::new()?;
   306→
   307→    let mut cmd = Command::cargo_bin("bivvy")?;
   308→    cmd.arg("init")
   309→        .arg("--non-interactive")
   310→        .current_dir(&temp)
   311→        .assert()
   312→        .success();
   313→
   314→    assert!(temp.path().join(".bivvy/config.yml").exists());
   315→    Ok(())
   316→}
   317→```
   318→
   319→### Test Utilities
   320→
   321→Create helpers in `tests/common/mod.rs`:
   322→
   323→```rust
   324→use tempfile::TempDir;
   325→
   326→pub fn setup_project(config: &str) -> Result<TempDir, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
   327→    let temp = TempDir::new()?;
   328→    std::fs::create_dir_all(temp.path().join(".bivvy"))?;
   329→    std::fs::write(temp.path().join(".bivvy/config.yml"), config)?;
   330→    Ok(temp)
   331→}
   332→```

   334→## Git Workflow
   335→
   336→### Commit Message Format
   337→
   338→<commit-format>
   339→  <subject>
   340→    <rule>Imperative mood ("Add feature" not "Added feature")</rule>
   341→    <rule>50 characters or less</rule>
   342→    <rule>Capitalize first letter</rule>
   343→    <rule>No period at the end</rule>
   344→    <rule>No type prefixes (no "feat:", "fix:", etc.)</rule>
   345→  </subject>
   346→  <body>
   347→    <rule>Blank line between subject and body</rule>
   348→    <rule>Wrap at 72 characters</rule>
   349→    <rule>Explain what and why, not how</rule>
   350→  </body>
   351→</commit-format>
   352→
   353→```
   354→Add BivvyError enum with thiserror
   355→
   356→Centralizes error handling with typed variants for
   357→config parsing, template resolution, and execution
   358→failures. Each variant includes context for debugging.
   359→```
   360→
   361→## What NOT to Do
   362→
   363→<anti-patterns>
   364→  <anti-pattern>Straying from `plans/` unless addressing an open question</anti-pattern>
   365→  <anti-pattern>Over-engineering or adding features not in the plan</anti-pattern>
   366→  <anti-pattern>Creating the full project structure upfront</anti-pattern>
   367→  <anti-pattern>Committing without tests</anti-pattern>
   368→  <anti-pattern>Committing with failing tests</anti-pattern>
   369→  <anti-pattern>Skipping or disabling tests to make them pass</anti-pattern>
   370→  <anti-pattern>Large commits with multiple concerns</anti-pattern>
   371→  <anti-pattern>Using deprecated APIs (check dependency versions)</anti-pattern>
   372→</anti-patterns>

     2→title: CI Integration
     3→description: Integrating Bivvy lint with CI/CD pipelines
     4→---
     5→
     6→# CI Integration
     7→
     8→Bivvy's lint command supports SARIF output format, which is widely supported
     9→by CI/CD systems and IDEs for displaying static analysis results.
    10→
    11→## GitHub Actions
    12→
    13→Upload SARIF results to GitHub Code Scanning:
    14→
    15→```yaml
    16→- name: Lint Bivvy config
    17→  run: bivvy lint --format=sarif > bivvy.sarif
    18→
    19→- uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2
    20→  with:
    21→    sarif_file: bivvy.sarif
    22→```
    23→
    24→## GitLab CI
    25→
    26→Export lint results as a report artifact:
    27→
    28→```yaml
    29→lint:
    30→  script:
    31→    - bivvy lint --format=json > bivvy-lint.json
    32→  artifacts:
    33→    reports:
    34→      codequality: bivvy-lint.json
    35→```
    36→
    37→## VS Code
    38→
    39→Use the [SARIF Viewer extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=MS-SarifVSCode.sarif-viewer)
    40→to view lint results directly in your editor:
    41→
    42→1. Install the SARIF Viewer extension
    43→2. Run `bivvy lint --format=sarif > .bivvy/lint.sarif`
    44→3. Open the SARIF file to see issues in the editor
    45→
    46→## Running Bivvy in CI
    47→
    48→Beyond linting, you can run Bivvy itself in CI to set up your test
    49→environment. Bivvy auto-detects CI environments (via `CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS`,
    50→and other common variables) and automatically forces non-interactive mode:
    51→
    52→```yaml
    53→# GitHub Actions
    54→- name: Setup environment
    55→  run: bivvy run --env ci
    56→```
    57→
    58→In CI mode, the workflow progress bar is suppressed to avoid noisy output
    59→in log-based environments. You can also explicitly pass `--non-interactive`
    60→or `--ci` to force this behavior outside auto-detected CI.
    61→
    62→### Provided requirements
    63→
    64→CI pipelines typically manage services (databases, caches) outside of
    65→Bivvy. Use `provided_requirements` to skip gap checks for tools that
    66→are already available:
    67→
    68→```yaml
    69→# .bivvy/config.yml
    70→settings:
    71→  environments:
    72→    ci:
    73→      provided_requirements:
    74→        - postgres-server
    75→        - redis-server
    76→        - docker
    77→```
    78→
    79→This prevents Bivvy from trying to install or start services that the
    80→pipeline already provides.
    81→
    82→### Environment-specific workflows
    83→
    84→You can also set a `default_workflow` for CI to run a different set of
    85→steps:
    86→
    87→```yaml
    88→settings:
    89→  environments:
    90→    ci:
    91→      default_workflow: ci
    92→      provided_requirements:
    93→        - postgres-server
    94→
    95→workflows:
    96→  ci:
    97→    description: "CI setup (no prompts)"
    98→    steps: [deps, database, migrations]
    99→    settings:
   100→      non_interactive: true
   101→```
   102→
   103→See [Environments](../configuration/environments.md) for the full
   104→environment configuration reference.
   105→
   106→## Exit Codes
   107→
   108→The lint command returns:
   109→- `0` - No errors (warnings allowed)
   110→- `1` - One or more errors found
   111→- `2` - Configuration loading error
   112→
   113→Use `--strict` to treat warnings as errors.
   114→

     2→title: bivvy run
     3→description: Run setup workflow
     4→---
     5→
     6→# bivvy run
     7→
     8→The main command to run your setup workflow.
     9→
    10→## Usage
    11→
    12→```bash
    13→bivvy
    14→```
    15→
    16→```bash
    17→bivvy run
    18→```
    19→
    20→```bash
    21→bivvy run -w ci
    22→```
    23→
    24→## Options
    25→
    26→| Option | Short | Description |
    27→|--------|-------|-------------|
    28→| `--workflow` | `-w` | Workflow to run (default: "default") |
    29→| `--only` | | Run only specified steps (comma-separated) |
    30→| `--skip` | | Skip specified steps (comma-separated) |
    31→| `--skip-behavior` | | How to handle skipped dependencies |
    32→| `--force` | `-f` | Force re-run of specified steps |
    33→| `--resume` | | Resume interrupted run |
    34→| `--save-preferences` | | Save prompt answers |
    35→| `--dry-run` | | Preview without executing |
    36→| `--env` | `-e` | Set active environment (e.g., `ci`, `staging`) |
    37→| `--non-interactive` | | Use defaults, no prompts |
    38→| `--ci` | | Deprecated: use `--non-interactive` instead |
    39→
    40→## Skip Behaviors
    41→
    42→When using `--skip`, you can control how dependents are handled:
    43→
    44→- `skip_with_dependents` (default): Skip the step and all its dependents
    45→- `skip_only`: Skip only this step, attempt to run dependents
    46→- `run_anyway`: Don't actually skip, run the step anyway
    47→
    48→## Examples
    49→
    50→Run only database setup:
    51→
    52→```bash
    53→bivvy run --only=database
    54→```
    55→
    56→Skip seeds step:
    57→
    58→```bash
    59→bivvy run --skip=seeds
    60→```
    61→
    62→Force re-run of node_deps:
    63→
    64→```bash
    65→bivvy run --force=node_deps
    66→```
    67→
    68→Preview what would run:
    69→
    70→```bash
    71→bivvy run --dry-run
    72→```
    73→
    74→Run with a specific environment:
    75→
    76→```bash
    77→bivvy run --env staging
    78→```
    79→
    80→Non-interactive mode:
    81→
    82→```bash
    83→bivvy run --non-interactive
    84→```
    85→
    86→Run with a specific workflow:
    87→
    88→```bash
    89→bivvy run --workflow=production
    90→```
    91→
    92→## Exit Codes
    93→
    94→| Code | Meaning |
    95→|------|---------|
    96→| 0 | All steps completed successfully |
    97→| 1 | One or more steps failed |
    98→| 2 | Configuration not found |
    99→| 130 | Interrupted (Ctrl+C) |
   100→

1→# Settings
     2→
     3→Global settings control Bivvy's behavior across all workflows.
     4→
     5→## Basic Settings
     6→
     7→```yaml
     8→settings:
     9→  default_output: verbose  # verbose | quiet | silent
    10→  logging: false
    11→  log_path: "logs/bivvy.log"
    12→```
    13→
    14→## Output Modes
    15→
    16→| Mode | Description |
    17→|------|-------------|
    18→| `verbose` | Show all output (default) |
    19→| `quiet` | Show only step names and errors |
    20→| `silent` | Show only errors |
    21→
    22→Override per-run:
    23→
    24→```bash
    25→bivvy --verbose
    26→```
    27→
    28→```bash
    29→bivvy --quiet
    30→```
    31→
    32→```bash
    33→bivvy --silent
    34→```
    35→
    36→## Global Environment Variables
    37→
    38→Set environment variables for all steps:
    39→
    40→```yaml
    41→settings:
    42→  env:
    43→    RAILS_ENV: development
    44→    DEBUG: "true"
    45→```
    46→
    47→## Parallel Execution
    48→
    49→```yaml
    50→settings:
    51→  parallel: true      # Enable parallel execution
    52→  max_parallel: 4     # Maximum concurrent steps (default: 4)
    53→```
    54→
    55→## History Retention
    56→
    57→```yaml
    58→settings:
    59→  history_retention: 50  # Keep last 50 runs (default)
    60→```
    61→
    62→## Fail Fast
    63→
    64→Stop workflow on first failure:
    65→
    66→```yaml
    67→settings:
    68→  fail_fast: true  # Stop on first error (default: true)
    69→```
    70→
    71→## Skip Behavior
    72→
    73→How to handle dependencies of skipped steps:
    74→
    75→```yaml
    76→settings:
    77→  skip_behavior: skip_with_dependents  # Also skip dependent steps
    78→  # skip_behavior: run_dependents      # Still try to run dependents
    79→```
    80→
    81→## Default Environment
    82→
    83→Set the environment used when `--env` is not provided and no environment
    84→is auto-detected:
    85→
    86→```yaml
    87→settings:
    88→  default_environment: staging
    89→```
    90→
    91→If omitted, Bivvy falls back to auto-detection and then to `development`.
    92→
    93→## Environments
    94→
    95→Define custom environments with detection rules, default workflows, and
    96→provided requirements:
    97→
    98→```yaml
    99→settings:
   100→  environments:
   101→    staging:
   102→      detect:
   103→        - env: DEPLOY_ENV
   104→          value: staging
   105→      default_workflow: staging
   106→      provided_requirements:
   107→        - postgres-server
   108→        - redis-server
   109→
   110→    review_app:
   111→      detect:
   112→        - env: REVIEW_APP
   113→      provided_requirements:
   114→        - docker
   115→```
   116→
   117→| Field | Type | Description |
   118→|-------|------|-------------|
   119→| `detect` | list | Environment variable rules for auto-detection |
   120→| `default_workflow` | string | Workflow to use when this environment is active |
   121→| `provided_requirements` | list | Requirements assumed satisfied (skip gap checks) |
   122→
   123→Each detect rule checks a single env var. Omit `value` to match on
   124→presence alone.
   125→
   126→See [Environments](environments.md) for the full guide.
   127→

## Comprehensive Exploration Report: Bivvy Rust Project

I've conducted a thorough analysis of the Bivvy project. Here's what I found:

### 1. Overall Project Structure

**Source Layout:**
- `/src/cli/` - CLI argument parsing and command implementations
- `/src/ui/` - User interface components (output modes, spinners, prompts, tables)
- `/src/config/` - Configuration schema and loading
- `/src/lint/` - Linting rules and formatters
- `/src/error.rs` - Error types
- `/src/runner/` - Workflow execution engine
- `/src/registry/` - Template registry
- `/src/state/` - Session and run history tracking
- `/src/steps/` - Step execution logic
- `/src/shell/` - Shell command execution
- `/src/requirements/` - Requirement checking and installation
- `/src/detection/` - Environment detection
- Other support modules: cache, feedback, session, updates, etc.

---

### 2. Output & Formatting System

**OutputMode Enum** (src/ui/output.rs):
- `Verbose` - Shows all output including command output
- `Normal` - Default, shows progress and status
- `Quiet` - Minimal output (spinners + final status)
- `Silent` - Show nothing except errors

**Configuration Integration:**
- Config schema (src/config/schema.rs) has `Settings.default_output: OutputMode`
- Defaults to `OutputMode::Verbose`
- CLI flags override config: `--verbose`, `--quiet` flags set OutputMode
- Run command applies config default when no CLI flag given (line 131-132 in run.rs)

**Output Writer** (src/ui/output.rs):
- Simple `Output` struct wrapping `OutputMode`
- Methods: `println()`, `command_output()`
- Respects mode before printing

**Existing Format Support in Lint Command:**
- `--format` flag with options: `human`, `json`, `sarif`
- Already implements SARIF output! (src/lint/output/sarif.rs)
- JSON formatter for structured output
- Human-readable formatter with colors

---

### 3. Error Reporting & Formatting

**BivvyError Enum** (src/error.rs) using `thiserror`:
- `ConfigNotFound`, `ConfigParseError`, `ConfigValidationError`
- `UnknownTemplate`, `CircularDependency`
- `StepExecutionError`, `CommandFailed`
- `RequirementMissing`, `RequirementCheckFailed`
- `ShellError`
- `Io` (std::io::Error)
- `Other` (anyhow::Error)

All errors provide context and actionable messages. Error messages displayed via `ui.error()` in main.rs line 72.

---

### 4. CLI Argument Parsing (clap derive)

**Main Cli Struct** (src/cli/args.rs):
```rust
pub struct Cli {
    #[arg(short, long, global = true)]
    pub config: Option<PathBuf>,
    
    #[arg(short, long, global = true)]
    pub project: Option<PathBuf>,
    
    #[arg(short, long, global = true)]
    pub verbose: bool,           // Sets OutputMode::Verbose
    
    #[arg(short, long, global = true)]
    pub quiet: bool,             // Sets OutputMode::Quiet
    
    #[arg(long, global = true)]
    pub no_color: bool,
    
    #[arg(long, global = true)]
    pub debug: bool,
}
```

**LintArgs Subcommand:**
```rust
pub struct LintArgs {
    #[arg(long, default_value = "human")]
    pub format: String,          // human | json | sarif
    
    #[arg(long)]
    pub fix: bool,
    
    #[arg(long)]
    pub strict: bool,
}
```

**Other relevant args with output flags:**
- `StatusArgs` - has `json` flag
- `ListArgs` - has `json` flag
- `LastArgs` - has `json`, `output` flags
- `HistoryArgs` - has `json` flag
- `ConfigArgs` - has `json`, `yaml` flags

---

### 5. Configuration Schema

**Settings Struct** (src/config/schema.rs):
```rust
pub struct Settings {
    /// Default output mode: verbose, quiet, silent
    #[serde(default = "default_output")]
    pub default_output: OutputMode,
    
    pub logging: bool,
    pub log_path: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub env: HashMap<String, String>,
    // ... other fields
}
```

**OutputMode Enum** (in schema):
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum OutputMode {
    #[default]
    Verbose,
    Quiet,
    Silent,
}
```

Example config:
```yaml
app_name: MyApp
settings:
  default_output: verbose  # or quiet, silent
  logging: false
```

---

### 6. Existing Tests for Output Formatting

**Integration tests** (tests/cli_test.rs):
- `cli_no_args_runs_default()` - validates output
- `cli_run_with_dry_run()` - expects "dry-run mode" in output
- `cli_status_shows_steps()` - expects "Steps:" in output
- `cli_list_shows_steps_and_workflows()` - multi-line output
- `cli_lint_validates_config()` - expects "Configuration is valid!"

**Unit tests** (src/ui/output.rs):
- `output_mode_from_str()` - parsing
- `output_mode_shows_command_output()` - mode behavior
- `output_mode_shows_spinners()`
- `output_mode_shows_status()`
- Config mode conversion tests

**Lint formatter tests** (src/lint/output/json.rs):
- `produces_valid_json()` - JSON structure validation
- `includes_location_when_present()` - file/line/column handling
- `summary_counts_by_severity()` - error/warning/hint counts

---

### 7. GitHub Actions Integration Context

**CI Workflow** (.github/workflows/test.yml):
- Runs `bivvy run --workflow ci --non-interactive --verbose`
- Coverage badge generation
- Uses `schneegans/dynamic-badges-action`

**Build Workflow** (.github/workflows/build.yml):
- Multi-platform builds (linux-x64, linux-arm64, macos, windows-x64)
- Artifacts uploaded
- Reusable workflow

**Lint in docs/commands/lint.md**:
- References `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2`
- Shows SARIF output as integration point for GitHub

---

### 8. Key Architectural Insights

**Output Mode Flow:**
1. CLI flags (`--verbose`, `--quiet`) determine initial `OutputMode`
2. If no flag → defaults to `OutputMode::Normal`
3. Commands check `ui.output_mode() == OutputMode::Normal`
4. If true, they apply `config.settings.default_output`
5. Commands can call `ui.set_output_mode()` to change at runtime

**Formatter Pattern:**
- `LintFormatter` trait with implementations (Human, Json, Sarif)
- Formatters write to `&mut W: Write`
- Lint command selects formatter based on `args.format`
- No centralized formatter registry yet

**Error Output:**
- Errors printed via `ui.error()` which respects output mode
- Uses structured error types from `BivvyError` enum
- Context preservation for debugging

**UI Abstraction:**
- `UserInterface` trait for mocking in tests
- `TerminalUI` for interactive use
- `NonInteractiveUI` for CI
- `MockUI` for testing

---

### 9. Ready for GitHub Actions Output Formatter

The project is well-positioned for a GitHub Actions output formatter feature:

✅ **Existing SARIF support** - Already supports SARIF format for GitHub Code Scanning
✅ **Structured error handling** - Typed error variants with context
✅ **Formatter pattern** - Extensible trait-based formatter system
✅ **Configuration hooks** - Can add to `Settings` struct
✅ **CLI arg pattern** - Easy to add `--format github-actions` flag
✅ **Test infrastructure** - Comprehensive tests for output validation
✅ **Separation of concerns** - Output generation isolated from business logic
✅ **Environment detection** - Already detects CI environments (`is_ci()` in shell/platform.rs)

**Key Files to Integrate With:**
- `/src/lint/output/` - For formatter implementation
- `/src/cli/args.rs` - For CLI argument
- `/src/config/schema.rs` - For config option
- `/src/ui/output.rs` - For output mode handling
- Tests in `tests/cli_test.rs` and specific formatter test modules

## Summary of Findings

I've thoroughly reviewed the Bivvy codebase and documentation. Here's what I've discovered:

### Project Overview

**Bivvy** is a Rust-based CLI tool for cross-language development environment setup automation. It replaces ad-hoc `bin/setup` scripts with declarative YAML configuration, state tracking, and a polished CLI experience.

**Key Architecture Principles:**
- Declarative orchestrator using a Template Registry (not hardcoded language logic)
- Optional pre-defined YAML templates during initialization
- User overrides at every level
- State tracking for smart re-runs
- Support for multiple platforms (macOS, Linux, Windows) in both 32-bit and 64-bit

### Existing Output & Format System

The project already has a sophisticated output formatting system in place:

1. **Lint Output Formatters** (`src/lint/output/`):
   - `HumanFormatter` - human-readable terminal output
   - `JsonFormatter` - machine-parseable JSON format
   - `SarifFormatter` - SARIF 2.1.0 format (Static Analysis Results Interchange Format)

2. **Lint Command** (`src/cli/commands/lint.rs`):
   - Already supports `--format=human|json|sarif` flag
   - Current implementation handles format selection in the `format_output()` method (line 61-80)
   - Tests exist for JSON and SARIF formats

3. **Run Command Output Mode** (`src/ui/output.rs`):
   - Separate concept: `OutputMode` enum with Verbose, Normal, Quiet, Silent
   - Controls verbosity of step execution output
   - Applied at configuration level via `default_output` setting

### CI Integration Documentation

The project already documents GitHub Actions integration:
- **docs/guides/ci-integration.md** shows GitHub Actions SARIF upload workflow
- Documents environment auto-detection for CI (`GITHUB_ACTIONS` env var)
- Uses `--non-interactive` flag for CI runs
- Documents `provided_requirements` for CI-managed services

### Key Existing Features

1. **Secret Masking** - Already masks sensitive values like `*_KEY`, `*_SECRET`, `*_TOKEN`
2. **Environment Detection** - Auto-detects CI from environment variables
3. **Configuration** - Settings schema supports:
   - `default_output: verbose | quiet | silent`
   - Environment-specific workflows
   - `non_interactive` mode flag

### Development Workflow

The project follows a strict test-first development workflow defined in `.claude/bivvy-dev-workflow.md`:

1. **Specification** - Write failing tests first
2. **Implementation** - Minimum code to pass tests
3. **Documentation** - Rustdoc + user-facing docs + source READMEs
4. **Linting** - `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
5. **Testing** - Full test suite: `cargo test --all-features` (NO filtering, must run ALL tests)
6. **Build** - Both debug and release builds
7. **Commit** - Atomic commits with code + tests + docs

**Critical Rule:** Always run `cargo test --all-features` without any filters. Output must show "0 filtered out".

### Documentation Structure

Two distinct audiences with strict boundaries:

1. **User-Facing** (`docs/`)
   - Starlight website pages
   - Written for end users
   - Covers commands, configuration, guides, templates

2. **Developer-Facing** (`src/`)
   - Rustdoc comments (`///` and `//!`)
   - Source READMEs for subsystem design
   - Focus on "why" and "how it fits together"

### Related Commands & Configurations

- **`bivvy lint --format=sarif`** - Already outputs SARIF format
- **`bivvy run --non-interactive`** - Already forces non-interactive mode
- **`bivvy run --env ci`** - Supports environment-specific workflows
- **`default_output` setting** - Configurable at YAML level

### Opportunity for GitHub Actions Formatter

The request to add a **GitHub Actions formatter** would fit naturally into this existing architecture:

1. **It's an output format**, not an output mode (like the existing JSON/SARIF formatters)
2. **GitHub Actions format** = `::notice::`, `::warning::`, `::error::` workflow commands
3. Could be added to the `OutputFormat` enum in `src/lint/output/mod.rs`
4. Could have a `GitHubActionsFormatter` struct alongside existing formatters
5. Would be used in `lint` command's `format_output()` method
6. Could optionally be extended to the `run` command for step output formatting
7. Already documented integration path in `docs/guides/ci-integration.md`

### Testing & Coverage Requirements

- Minimum 90% code coverage required
- Uses `insta` for snapshot testing
- Uses `assert_cmd` and `tempfile` for integration tests
- Must test both happy path and error cases

---

## Conclusion

Bivvy is a well-architected, mature Rust CLI tool with clear development practices, comprehensive documentation, and an extensible output formatting system. The GitHub Actions formatter feature would be a natural addition that integrates seamlessly with the existing architecture and development workflow.

Design an implementation plan for adding a GitHub Actions output formatter to the Bivvy lint command.

## Context

Bivvy is a Rust CLI tool with a lint command (`bivvy lint`) that validates YAML configuration. The lint system already has:

1. **Formatter trait** (`LintFormatter`) in `src/lint/output/mod.rs` with `format()` method taking `&[LintDiagnostic]` and `&mut W: Write`
2. **Three existing formatters**: `HumanFormatter`, `JsonFormatter`, `SarifFormatter`
3. **OutputFormat enum** in `src/lint/output/mod.rs`: `Human`, `Json`, `Sarif`
4. **CLI arg**: `--format` on LintArgs accepting a string, matched in `format_output()` in `src/cli/commands/lint.rs`
5. **LintDiagnostic** has: `rule_id: RuleId`, `severity: Severity`, `message: String`, `span: Option<Span>`, `suggestion: Option<String>`, `related: Vec<RelatedInfo>`
6. **Span** has: `file: PathBuf`, `start_line: usize`, `start_col: usize`
7. **Severity** has: `Hint`, `Warning`, `Error`

The lint command's `format_output()` method selects formatter based on `self.args.format.as_str()` matching "json", "sarif", or defaulting to human.

The lint command output section in `execute()` has special handling: for "human" format it routes lines through `ui.error()`/`ui.warning()`/`ui.message()`, for JSON/SARIF it outputs as-is via `ui.message()`.

## GitHub Actions Workflow Commands

GitHub Actions supports workflow commands as special stdout annotations:
- `::error file={name},line={line},col={col}::{message}`
- `::warning file={name},line={line},col={col}::{message}`
- `::notice file={name},line={line},col={col}::{message}`

Optional parameters: `file`, `line`, `endLine`, `col`, `endColumn`, `title`

## Requirements

Add `--format github-actions` (or `--format gha`) to the lint command that outputs `::error::`, `::warning::`, and `::notice::` annotations.

## Design Constraints

- Follow existing patterns exactly (new file `src/lint/output/gha.rs`, implement `LintFormatter` trait)
- Update the `OutputFormat` enum
- Update `format_output()` match and the output section in `execute()`
- Update `LintArgs` help text to mention the new format
- Add comprehensive tests following existing test patterns
- Update re-exports in `src/lint/mod.rs`
- Update docs if applicable

Design the complete implementation plan with file-by-file changes.

     6→# bivvy lint
     7→
     8→Validates your Bivvy configuration without executing anything.
     9→
    10→## Usage
    11→
    12→```bash
    13→bivvy lint
    14→```
    15→
    16→```bash
    17→bivvy lint --format=json
    18→```
    19→
    20→```bash
    21→bivvy lint --format=sarif

    23→
    24→```bash

    30→```
    31→
    32→## Exit Codes
    33→
    34→| Code | Meaning |
    35→|------|---------|
    36→| 0 | No errors (warnings OK) |
    37→| 1 | Errors found |
    38→| 2 | No configuration found |
    39→
    40→With `--strict`, warnings also cause exit code 1.
    41→
    42→## Example Output
    43→
    44→### Valid Configuration
    45→
    46→```
    47→Configuration is valid!
    48→```
    49→
    50→### Invalid Configuration
    51→
    52→```
    53→error [default]: Workflow references unknown step 'nonexistent'
    54→
    55→Found 1 error(s)
    56→```
    57→
    58→## Integration
    59→
    60→### VS Code
    61→
    62→Use the SARIF Viewer extension:
    63→
    64→```bash
    65→bivvy lint --format=sarif > bivvy.sarif
    66→```
    67→
    68→### GitHub Actions
    69→
    70→```yaml
    71→- name: Lint Bivvy config
    72→  run: bivvy lint --format=sarif > bivvy.sarif
    73→- uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2
    74→  with:
    75→    sarif_file: bivvy.sarif
    76→```
    77→

     3→description: Integrating Bivvy lint with CI/CD pipelines
     4→---
     5→
     6→# CI Integration
     7→
     8→Bivvy's lint command supports SARIF output format, which is widely supported
     9→by CI/CD systems and IDEs for displaying static analysis results.
    10→
    11→## GitHub Actions
    12→
    13→Upload SARIF results to GitHub Code Scanning:
    14→
    15→```yaml
    16→- name: Lint Bivvy config
    17→  run: bivvy lint --format=sarif > bivvy.sarif
    18→
    19→- uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2
    20→  with:
    21→    sarif_file: bivvy.sarif
    22→```
    23→
    24→## GitLab CI
    25→
    26→Export lint results as a report artifact:
    27→
    28→```yaml
    29→lint:
    30→  script:
    31→    - bivvy lint --format=json > bivvy-lint.json
    32→  artifacts:
    33→    reports:
    34→      codequality: bivvy-lint.json
    35→```
    36→
    37→## VS Code
    38→
    39→Use the [SARIF Viewer extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=MS-SarifVSCode.sarif-viewer)
    40→to view lint results directly in your editor:
    41→
    42→1. Install the SARIF Viewer extension
    43→2. Run `bivvy lint --format=sarif > .bivvy/lint.sarif`
    44→3. Open the SARIF file to see issues in the editor
    45→
    46→## Running Bivvy in CI
    47→
    48→Beyond linting, you can run Bivvy itself in CI to set up your test
    49→environment. Bivvy auto-detects CI environments (via `CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS`,
    50→and other common variables) and automatically forces non-interactive mode:
    51→
    52→```yaml
    53→# GitHub Actions
    54→- name: Setup environment
    55→  run: bivvy run --env ci
    56→```
    57→
    58→In CI mode, the workflow progress bar is suppressed to avoid noisy output
    59→in log-based environments. You can also explicitly pass `--non-interactive`
    60→or `--ci` to force this behavior outside auto-detected CI.
    61→
    62→### Provided requirements
    63→
    64→CI pipelines typically manage services (databases, caches) outside of
    65→Bivvy. Use `provided_requirements` to skip gap checks for tools that
    66→are already available:
    67→
    68→```yaml
    69→# .bivvy/config.yml
    70→settings:
    71→  environments:
    72→    ci:
    73→      provided_requirements:
    74→        - postgres-server
    75→        - redis-server
    76→        - docker
    77→```
    78→
    79→This prevents Bivvy from trying to install or start services that the
    80→pipeline already provides.
    81→
    82→### Environment-specific workflows
    83→
    84→You can also set a `default_workflow` for CI to run a different set of
    85→steps:
    86→
    87→```yaml
    88→settings:
    89→  environments:
    90→    ci:
    91→      default_workflow: ci
    92→      provided_requirements:
    93→        - postgres-server
    94→
    95→workflows:
    96→  ci:
    97→    description: "CI setup (no prompts)"
    98→    steps: [deps, database, migrations]
    99→    settings:
   100→      non_interactive: true
   101→```
   102→
   103→See [Environments](../configuration/environments.md) for the full
   104→environment configuration reference.
   105→
   106→## Exit Codes
   107→
   108→The lint command returns:
   109→- `0` - No errors (warnings allowed)
   110→- `1` - One or more errors found
   111→- `2` - Configuration loading error
   112→
   113→Use `--strict` to treat warnings as errors.
   114→

Design an implementation plan for adding a GitHub Actions output formatter to the Bivvy lint command.

## Context

Bivvy is a Rust CLI tool with a lint command (`bivvy lint`) that validates YAML configuration. The lint system already has:

1. **Formatter trait** (`LintFormatter`) in `src/lint/output/mod.rs` with `format()` method taking `&[LintDiagnostic]` and `&mut W: Write`
2. **Three existing formatters**: `HumanFormatter`, `JsonFormatter`, `SarifFormatter`
3. **OutputFormat enum** in `src/lint/output/mod.rs`: `Human`, `Json`, `Sarif`
4. **CLI arg**: `--format` on LintArgs accepting a string, matched in `format_output()` in `src/cli/commands/lint.rs`
5. **LintDiagnostic** has: `rule_id: RuleId`, `severity: Severity`, `message: String`, `span: Option<Span>`, `suggestion: Option<String>`, `related: Vec<RelatedInfo>`
6. **Span** has: `file: PathBuf`, `start_line: usize`, `start_col: usize`
7. **Severity** has: `Hint`, `Warning`, `Error`

The lint command's `format_output()` method selects formatter based on `self.args.format.as_str()` matching "json", "sarif", or defaulting to human.

The lint command output section in `execute()` has special handling: for "human" format it routes lines through `ui.error()`/`ui.warning()`/`ui.message()`, for JSON/SARIF it outputs as-is via `ui.message()`.

## GitHub Actions Workflow Commands

GitHub Actions supports workflow commands as special stdout annotations:
- `::error file={name},line={line},col={col}::{message}`
- `::warning file={name},line={line},col={col}::{message}`
- `::notice file={name},line={line},col={col}::{message}`

Optional parameters: `file`, `line`, `endLine`, `col`, `endColumn`, `title`

## Requirements

Add `--format github-actions` (or `--format gha`) to the lint command that outputs `::error::`, `::warning::`, and `::notice::` annotations.

## Design Constraints

- Follow existing patterns exactly (new file `src/lint/output/gha.rs`, implement `LintFormatter` trait)
- Update the `OutputFormat` enum
- Update `format_output()` match and the output section in `execute()`
- Update `LintArgs` help text to mention the new format
- Add comprehensive tests following existing test patterns
- Update re-exports in `src/lint/mod.rs`
- Update docs if applicable

Design the complete implementation plan with file-by-file changes.

# Plan: GitHub Actions Output Formatter for `bivvy lint`

## Context

The `bivvy lint` command validates YAML configuration and already supports three output formats (`human`, `json`, `sarif`) via the `LintFormatter` trait. CI users running `bivvy lint` in GitHub Actions currently must either parse human output or upload SARIF files. Adding native `::error::`/`::warning::`/`::notice::` workflow command output gives GitHub Actions users inline PR annotations with zero extra setup.

## Changes

### 1. Create `src/lint/output/gha.rs` — GHA formatter

New file implementing `LintFormatter`. Follows `JsonFormatter` pattern (unit struct, `new()`, `Default` impl).

- Maps `Severity::Error` → `::error`, `Warning` → `::warning`, `Hint` → `::notice`
- Emits one workflow command per diagnostic: `::error file=F,line=L,col=C,title=RULE::MESSAGE`
- Includes `file`, `line`, `col` from `Span` when present; skips `col` when 1; includes `endLine` when different from `start_line`; skips `endColumn` when `usize::MAX` sentinel
- Always emits `title=` with `rule_id`
- Appends suggestion and related info to message body with `%0A` separator

# bivvy lint

Validates your Bivvy configuration without executing anything.

## Usage

```bash
bivvy lint
```

```bash
bivvy lint --format=json
```

```bash
bivvy lint --format=sarif
```

```bash
bivvy lint --fix
```

```bash
bivvy lint --strict
```

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | No errors (warnings OK) |
| 1 | Errors found |
| 2 | No configuration found |

With `--strict`, warnings also cause exit code 1.

## Example Output

### Valid Configuration

```
Configuration is valid!
```

### Invalid Configuration

```
error [default]: Workflow references unknown step 'nonexistent'

Found 1 error(s)
```

## Integration

### VS Code

Use the SARIF Viewer extension:

```bash
bivvy lint --format=sarif > bivvy.sarif
```

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint Bivvy config
  run: bivvy lint --format=sarif > bivvy.sarif
- uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2
  with:
    sarif_file: bivvy.sarif
```

---
title: CI Integration
description: Integrating Bivvy lint with CI/CD pipelines
---

# CI Integration

Bivvy's lint command supports SARIF output format, which is widely supported
by CI/CD systems and IDEs for displaying static analysis results.

## GitHub Actions

Upload SARIF results to GitHub Code Scanning:

```yaml
- name: Lint Bivvy config
  run: bivvy lint --format=sarif > bivvy.sarif

- uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2
  with:
    sarif_file: bivvy.sarif
```

## GitLab CI

Export lint results as a report artifact:

```yaml
lint:
  script:
    - bivvy lint --format=json > bivvy-lint.json
  artifacts:
    reports:
      codequality: bivvy-lint.json
```

## VS Code

Use the [SARIF Viewer extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=MS-SarifVSCode.sarif-viewer)
to view lint results directly in your editor:

1. Install the SARIF Viewer extension
2. Run `bivvy lint --format=sarif > .bivvy/lint.sarif`
3. Open the SARIF file to see issues in the editor

## Running Bivvy in CI

Beyond linting, you can run Bivvy itself in CI to set up your test
environment. Bivvy auto-detects CI environments (via `CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS`,
and other common variables) and automatically forces non-interactive mode:

```yaml
# GitHub Actions
- name: Setup environment
  run: bivvy run --env ci
```

In CI mode, the workflow progress bar is suppressed to avoid noisy output
in log-based environments. You can also explicitly pass `--non-interactive`
or `--ci` to force this behavior outside auto-detected CI.

### Provided requirements

CI pipelines typically manage services (databases, caches) outside of
Bivvy. Use `provided_requirements` to skip gap checks for tools that
are already available:

```yaml
# .bivvy/config.yml
settings:
  environments:
    ci:
      provided_requirements:
        - postgres-server
        - redis-server
        - docker
```

This prevents Bivvy from trying to install or start services that the
pipeline already provides.

### Environment-specific workflows

You can also set a `default_workflow` for CI to run a different set of
steps:

```yaml
settings:
  environments:
    ci:
      default_workflow: ci
      provided_requirements:
        - postgres-server

workflows:
  ci:
    description: "CI setup (no prompts)"
    steps: [deps, database, migrations]
    settings:
      non_interactive: true
```

See [Environments](../configuration/environments.md) for the full
environment configuration reference.

## Exit Codes

The lint command returns:
- `0` - No errors (warnings allowed)
- `1` - One or more errors found
- `2` - Configuration loading error

Use `--strict` to treat warnings as errors.

tool_input.plan:
# Plan: GitHub Actions Output Formatter for `bivvy lint`

## Context

The `bivvy lint` command validates YAML configuration and already supports three output formats (`human`, `json`, `sarif`) via the `LintFormatter` trait. CI users running `bivvy lint` in GitHub Actions currently must either parse human output or upload SARIF files. Adding native `::error::`/`::warning::`/`::notice::` workflow command output gives GitHub Actions users inline PR annotations with zero extra setup.

## Changes

### 1. Create `src/lint/output/gha.rs` — GHA formatter

New file implementing `LintFormatter`. Follows `JsonFormatter` pattern (unit struct, `new()`, `Default` impl).

- Maps `Severity::Error` → `::error`, `Warning` → `::warning`, `Hint` → `::notice`
- Emits one workflow command per diagnostic: `::error file=F,line=L,col=C,title=RULE::MESSAGE`
- Includes `file`, `line`, `col` from `Span` when present; skips `col` when 1; includes `endLine` when different from `start_line`; skips `endColumn` when `usize::MAX` sentinel
- Always emits `title=` with `rule_id`
- Appends suggestion and related info to message body with `%0A` separator
- Escapes `%` → `%25`, `\r` → `%0D`, `\n` → `%0A` in message values
- No summary line (GitHub Actions shows annotation counts natively)
- ~15 unit tests covering: each severity, span present/absent, col=1 omission, endLine, title, suggestion, related info, escaping, empty diagnostics, multiple diagnostics

### 2. Update `src/lint/output/mod.rs`

- Add `pub mod gha;`
- Add `GithubActions` variant to `OutputFormat` enum
- Add `pub use gha::GhaFormatter;`

### 3. Update `src/lint/mod.rs`

- Add `GhaFormatter` to the re-export line

### 4. Update `src/cli/args.rs`

- Update `LintArgs.format` help text: `"Output format: human, json, sarif, github-actions (or gha)"`

### 5. Update `src/cli/commands/lint.rs`

- Add `GhaFormatter` to imports
- Add `"github-actions" | "gha"` match arm in `format_output()` creating `GhaFormatter::new()`
- No changes needed in `execute()` — existing `if self.args.format == "human"` logic already routes non-human formats through `ui.message()` as-is

# Plan: GitHub Actions Output Formatter for `bivvy lint`

## Context

The `bivvy lint` command validates YAML configuration and already supports three output formats (`human`, `json`, `sarif`) via the `LintFormatter` trait. CI users running `bivvy lint` in GitHub Actions currently must either parse human output or upload SARIF files. Adding native `::error::`/`::warning::`/`::notice::` workflow command output gives GitHub Actions users inline PR annotations with zero extra setup.

## Changes

### 1. Create `src/lint/output/gha.rs` — GHA formatter

New file implementing `LintFormatter`. Follows `JsonFormatter` pattern (unit struct, `new()`, `Default` impl).

- Maps `Severity::Error` → `::error`, `Warning` → `::warning`, `Hint` → `::notice`
- Emits one workflow command per diagnostic: `::error file=F,line=L,col=C,title=RULE::MESSAGE`
- Includes `file`, `line`, `col` from `Span` when present; skips `col` when 1; includes `endLine` when different from `start_line`; skips `endColumn` when `usize::MAX` sentinel
- Always emits `title=` with `rule_id`
- Appends suggestion and related info to message body with `%0A` separator
- Escapes `%` → `%25`, `\r` → `%0D`, `\n` → `%0A` in message values
- No summary line (GitHub Actions shows annotation counts natively)
- ~15 unit tests covering: each severity, span present/absent, col=1 omission, endLine, title, suggestion, related info, escaping, empty diagnostics, multiple diagnostics

- Add `pub mod gha;`
